When the dog responded so badly to the treatment, we decided to let nature take its course.

senses.definition: a hollow place or structure that a bird makes or chooses for laying its eggs in and sheltering its young

examples.x: sparrows building a nest of twigs and dry grass

senses.definition: a place where insects or other small creatures live and produce their young

examples.x: a wasps’ nest
a nest of mice
The snake will attack if disturbed inside its nest.

senses.definition: a secret place which is full of bad people and their activities

examples.x: a nest of thieves

senses.definition: the home, thought of as the safe place where parents bring up their children

examples.x: to leave the nest (= leave your parents’ home)

senses.definition: a group or set of similar things that are made to fit inside each other

examples.x: a nest of tables

senses.definition: to make yourself richer, especially at somebody else's expense, by spending money on yourself that should be spent on somebody/something else
to become able to fly and leave its nest
to leave home and live somewhere else

examples.x: Her children have flown the nest.

senses.definition: a difficult situation in which a lot of people get very angry

examples.x: His letter to the papers stirred up a real hornets' nest.

senses.definition: a discovery that seems interesting but is found to have no value
a very complicated situation

examples.x: This area of the law is a veritable mare’s nest.

senses.definition: an area of public land in a town or a city where people go to walk, play and relax

examples.x: Hyde Park
We went for a walk in the park.
A public park will be built around the complex.
a park bench
the park entrance/gates

senses.definition: an area of land used for a particular purpose

examples.x: a business/science park
a wildlife park
a park ranger
She lives in a trailer park in Tucson, Arizona.

senses.definition: (in the UK) an area of land, usually with fields and trees, attached to a large country house

examples.x: The cottage is set within the park of a country house.
The houses and parks in Georgian Sussex represented leisured society at its peak.

senses.definition: a piece of land for playing sports, especially baseball

examples.x: With a mighty swing he hit the ball right out of the park.

senses.definition: a football (soccer) or rugby field

examples.x: the fastest man on the park

senses.definition: the position of the gears in a car with automatic transmission (= a system that changes the gears by itself so the driver does not have to) in which they are locked so that the engine cannot send any power to the wheels

examples.x: She put the car in park, pulled out the key and got out.

senses.definition: a thing that is very easy to do or deal with

examples.x: The role isn't exactly a walk in the park.
The next game will be a walk in the park.

senses.definition: the point when somebody/something is best, most successful, strongest, etc.

examples.x: Traffic reaches its peak between 8 and 9 in the morning.
the peaks and troughs of married life
She's at the peak of her career.
Membership of the club has fallen from a peak of 600 people in 2022.

senses.definition: the pointed top of a mountain; a mountain with a pointed top

examples.x: a mountain peak
snow-capped/jagged peaks
The climbers made camp halfway up the peak.
We looked up at the rocky peaks towering above us.

senses.definition: any narrow and pointed shape, edge, etc.

examples.x: Whisk the egg whites into stiff peaks.
He combed his hair into a peak.

senses.definition: the stiff front part of a cap that sticks out above your eyes
an animal, a bird, etc. that you have at home for pleasure, rather than one that is kept for work or food

examples.x: Do you have any pets?
a pet dog/hamster
a family pet
exotic pets
pet food
Being a responsible pet owner means caring for your pet.
a pet shop (= where animals are sold as pets)
Keeping pigs as pets has become extremely popular.

senses.definition: a person who is given special attention by somebody, especially in a way that seems unfair to other people

examples.x: She's the teacher's pet.

senses.definition: used when speaking to somebody to show kind feelings or to be friendly

examples.x: What's wrong, pet?
Be a pet (= be kind) and post this letter for me.

senses.definition: an animal with pink, black or brown skin, short legs, a broad nose and a short curly tail. Pigs are kept on farms for their meat (called pork) or live in the wild.

examples.x: a pig farmer
Pigs were grunting and squealing in the yard.
to breed/rear pigs

senses.definition: a person who you find unpleasant or offensive; a person who you think is dirty or greedy

examples.x: Arrogant pig!
Don't be such a pig!
The greedy pig's eaten all the biscuits!
She made a pig of herself with the ice cream (= ate too much).
He's a real male chauvinist pig (= a man who does not think women are equal to men).
We cooked up a load of pasta and all made pigs of ourselves.

senses.definition: an offensive word for a police officer
to do something badly; to make a mess of something
if you buy a pig in a poke, you buy something without seeing it or knowing if it is good enough

examples.x: Buying online can mean buying a pig in a poke.

senses.definition: a difficult or unpleasant thing or task

examples.x: I've had a pig of a day.

senses.definition: used to show that you do not believe something will ever happen

examples.x: ‘With a bit of luck, we'll be finished by the end of the year.’ ‘Yes, and pigs might fly!’

senses.definition: to make small changes to something, especially its outside appearance, to try and hide the fact that it has problems

examples.x: The change of policy doesn't go far enough—it's just putting lipstick on a pig.

senses.definition: a living thing that grows in the earth and usually has a stem, leaves and roots, especially one that is smaller than a tree or bush

examples.x: All plants need light and water.
flowering plants
native/medicinal/wild plants
a tomato/potato plant
It's becoming more popular to grow plants organically.
The area is home to many rare plant species.
the animal and plant life of the area

senses.definition: a factory or place where power is produced or an industrial process takes place

examples.x: a nuclear power plant
a processing/manufacturing plant
Japanese car plants
a water treatment plant
a chemical/steel/coal plant

senses.definition: the large machines that are used in industrial processes

examples.x: The company has been investing in new plant and equipment.

senses.definition: something that somebody has deliberately placed among another person’s clothes or possessions in order to make them appear guilty of a crime

examples.x: He claimed that the drugs found in his house were a plant.

senses.definition: a person who joins a group of criminals or enemies in order to get and secretly report information about their activities
a small area of still water, especially one that is artificial

examples.x: a fish pond

senses.definition: the Atlantic Ocean

examples.x: He's relatively unknown on this side of the pond.
Critics across the pond have been queuing up to heap praise on the movie.

senses.definition: an important person (in a small community)
an animal that kills and eats other animals

examples.x: Some animals have no natural predators.
the relationship between predator and prey

senses.definition: a person or an organization that uses weaker people for their own advantage

examples.x: to protect domestic industry from foreign predators

senses.definition: an animal, a bird, etc. that is hunted, killed and eaten by another

examples.x: The lion will often stalk its prey for hours.
birds of prey (= birds that kill for food)

senses.definition: a person who is harmed or tricked by somebody, especially for dishonest purposes

examples.x: Socially isolated young people are easy prey for extremists.

senses.definition: to be killed and eaten by another animal or bird

examples.x: Many small birds and rodents fall prey to the domestic cat.

senses.definition: to be harmed or affected by something bad

examples.x: Since the attack, he had fallen prey to irrational fears.
She knew she must not fall prey to his charm.
The new government has fallen prey to corruption and fraud.
